### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ce9c7f990922652c190e6ebd96ec2a5550c5568` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T21:52Z

Head-sha: 4914d02fc26dd38a6f574345b14439049ffe3155
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34896 (claim premise 6960374559). The area summary on this PR is the dev summary. This comment is the L1 record.

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Part of #34896`, base `main`. Three paths, +31/-3:
- `docs/qa/scenarios/travel_expense.json`;
- the Build-half pin in `packages/qa/scenarios/test/dataset-cards.test.ts`;
- a `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset.

`@objectstack/scenarios` is not private, so the changeset is right. `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none` match a card-data and test change. Not governed, 34 lines.

**CI.** 36 success, 18 expected skips. `Check Changeset` timed out once (134372992675, cancelled), and its re-run 134393634220 is green on this head. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` and all ten `Test Core` shards are green.

**The ambiguity the card tests is kept.** The card asks "What is our total travel spend?" so that the answer is a question back. "travel spend" / 「差旅花费」 is a synonym of `trip_plan.estimated_spend` and `reimbursement.claimed_amount`, and of nothing else. I checked every word the new dataset brings under the exact-match rule (ADR-0149 D3 rule 1):
- the name and label `claim_lines` / "Claim lines";
- `line_amount` / "Line amount", with synonyms "line total" and 明细金额;
- `expense_type` / "Expense type", with synonym 费用类型.

None of them equals "travel spend" or 差旅花费 after normalization. So the question's match set is still exactly the two measures.

**The hole is closed.** The report sentence used to read "a report of travel spend by department and expense type" / 「统计差旅支出的报表」, with no dataset pinned, and that invited a build to declare its own "Travel spend" dataset. Now it reads "claim line amounts … built on the claim_lines dataset" / 「统计明细金额的报表,数据取自 claim_lines 数据集」, in both languages. The phrase is gone from the sentence. The other prompt text is byte-unchanged.

**The new dataset agrees with the card.**
- `claim_line` is in `expect.objects`. `expense_type` is a declared select on it (`minOptions: 3`). `amount` is one of the line's fields in the prompt ("a quantity, a unit amount and an amount").
- The descriptions are business definitions, not instructions. "every claim status counted, rejected ones included" is true of an unfiltered sum. "hotel, meals or airfare" is the prompt's own 住宿、餐补、机票.

**The pin.** The fixture gains `claim_lines` on `demotravel_claim_line`, with the same members and synonyms, and the passing run now lists its three checks. The "drop the last dataset" case now drops `claim_lines`, and the test expects exactly its three checks to fail. Dropping a whole dataset is still covered, now on the newest one.

**Closing condition.** The body keeps #34896 open until two fresh builds of the changed card give `dq_travel_spend` the same match set, and the seat approved both builds. That is the right test, because only a real build shows whether the prompt still invites a self-named dataset.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. `expect.dashboards` and `appNavTargets` still name `travel_spend_by_department`, so a build will likely label that dashboard "Travel spend by department". A dashboard is not in `list_datasets`, so this does not change the match set. If one of the two fresh builds still declares a "Travel spend" dataset behind the dashboard, this name is the next suspect.
- N2. The platform allows a relationship-path dimension (`claim.claimant.department`, declared in `include`), so a build may add a department dimension to `claim_lines`. Its label ("Department") does not collide with the question. The body's "a card dimension names a field of the base object" is the card checker's limit, and it is stated as such. Nothing is owed.

Next: o3-F lands, since the three aggregates are green. No seat L2 is owed. #34896 stays open for the two builds. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.
